source.anchor_kjv: Philip findeth Nathanael, and saith unto him, We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph. And Nathanael said unto him, Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth? Philip saith unto him, Come and see. Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him, and saith of him, Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile! Nathanael saith unto him, Whence knowest thou me? Jesus answered and said unto him, Before that Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee. Nathanael answered and saith unto him, Rabbi, thou art the Son of God; thou art the King of Israel. Jesus answered and said unto him, Because I said unto thee, I saw thee under the fig tree, believest thou? thou shalt see greater things than these. And he saith unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Hereafter ye shall see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man.
source.hook_line: A man insulted Jesus behind His back.
source.spoken_script: A man insulted Jesus behind His back. Jesus complimented him to his face. Philip told Nathanael the news: the Messiah — Jesus, of Nazareth. Nathanael's answer: "Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth?" Philip did not argue — he invited. Jesus spoke first: "Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile!" Nathanael asked: "Whence knowest thou me?" Jesus answered: "Before that Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee." A moment only heaven had seen — named. The doubt did not fade. It fell. Nathanael said: "Rabbi, thou art the Son of God; thou art the King of Israel." And Jesus went further: "Thou shalt see greater things than these... Hereafter ye shall see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man." That is Jacob's ladder — the one Jesus said He is, standing open, permanently. He is not offended by honest questions. He already sees you, under your fig tree. Come and see.

platforms.description:
John 1:45-51. Before Nathanael ever met Jesus, he doubted Him out loud. And Jesus did not argue.

Philip told him the news. Nathanael said, "Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth?" Philip saith unto him, "Come and see." He did not argue. He invited.

Then Jesus spoke first: "Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile!" Nathanael asked how Jesus knew him, and Jesus answered, "Before that Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee." (John 1:45-51, KJV)

A moment only heaven had seen, named out loud. The doubt did not fade. It fell. And Jesus promised him more: heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man. That is the ladder Jacob saw, and Jesus says it is Himself.

He is not offended by honest questions. He already sees you, wherever your fig tree is. Come and see.

redteam:
VERDICT: REVISE
- youtube_short description: "That is the ladder Jacob saw, and Jesus says it is Himself." Overclaim. John 1:51 echoes Jacob's ladder (Gen 28:12) but Jesus does not say "I am the ladder" in those words. Fix: "It echoes the ladder Jacob saw in Genesis 28."
- youtube_short description: "He did not argue. He invited." follows the Philip line but the pronoun could read as Jesus. Fix: "Philip did not argue. He invited."
- title (all): "insulted Jesus behind His back" - Nathanael doubted Nazareth before he met Jesus; he did not know Jesus was there. Honest but strong. Acceptable because the hook is true to the text (the doubt was about Jesus' hometown and given in His absence). Keep, but the description's first line already clarifies.
- facebook: "Jesus is not offended by honest questions" is a theological generalisation from one story. Fix: "Jesus met this honest question with welcome."
- youtube_long: present as a stub; not a posting target for a 60s short. No action.
- Verse quotes: all quoted phrases are verbatim KJV from the anchor. PASS on that gate.
